name: ScreenshotOne
description: A screenshot, PDF, and video API. Solo founder Dmytro Krasun. Pricing is subscriptions plus pay-as-you-go. No funding. A target of $50,000 a month is a goal, not a current figure.

mentions.evidence: Self-reported. Not independently checked. A late-September brief put it near $12,000 a month, from Starter Story. That note is not on this site. Indie Hackers, 5 March 2026, says over 800 paying customers and over $25,000 a month. SoloBiz, 27 October 2026, repeats more than $25,000 a month and more than 800 customers. The $25,000 figure is from March 2026, so it is not necessarily today's number.
mentions.indieAngle: An unsexy API that is easier to rent than to maintain.

whyItPrints: Developers pay so they do not have to keep a screenshot service running themselves.
whyThisMatters:
ScreenshotOne takes a URL and sends back a screenshot, a PDF, or a short video. Dmytro Krasun runs it alone. You can subscribe, or you can pay for what you use. He has not raised. Fifty thousand a month is a target he has said out loud, not a figure on a payment account.

Two public write-ups carry the same claim. Indie Hackers in March 2026 says more than eight hundred paying customers and more than twenty-five thousand a month. SoloBiz in late October 2026 repeats that. The monthly figure is the March one, so it is not a sync from this morning. A late-September brief had a lower number, from Starter Story, and that note never became a page here. I am not backfilling a mention I do not have.

You pay so the screenshot job is someone else's server.

Pay-as-you-go sits next to the subscription. No funding is part of the recap. The fifty-thousand target is his, and it is not the March figure. SoloBiz is a retelling of the interview, not a new sync.
